newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends lower on arbitrage trading.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends lower on arbitrage trading.

text.p: SIMEX 225-share Nikkei index futures ended lower on Thursday after a bout of arbitrage unwinding, dealers said.
"Trading was mostly range-bound today. The main players were the arbitrageuers unwinding their positions," said a dealer with a Japanese institution.
Dealers said the market was underpinned by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita's comments made during the annual bankers meeting in Japan.
"He did not say anything new but his comments that BOJ's monetary policy will continue to be aimed at strengthening an economic recovery was supportive," the dealer said.
The benchmark September Nikkei futures ended 30 points down at 20,180 after hitting a low of 20,080.
Dealers said a U.S. institution was among the main sellers while an Asian insitution was seen buying.
Good support and resistance were pegged at 20,100 and 20,220 respectively, dealers said.
